title: 1985 AHSME Problem 7
statement: In some computer languages (such as APL), when there are no parentheses in an algebraic expression, the operations are grouped from right to left. Thus, \(a\times b-c\) in such languages means the same as \(a(b-c)\) in ordinary algebraic notation. If \(a\div b-c+d\) is evaluated in such a language, the result in ordinary algebraic notation would be

solutions.text:
Grouping from the right first gives \(c+d.\) Subtracting this result from \(b\) gives \(b-(c+d)=b-c-d.\) Finally, dividing \(a\) by that quantity gives \(\frac{a}{b-c-d}.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Next subtract that result from \(b,\) and only then divide \(a\)
